Aristaenetus.fact: Aristaenetus (Greek: Ἀρισταίνετος) was an ancient Greek epistolographer who flourished in the 5th or 6th century.

Aristaenetus.subject: Computer & IT
Aristaenetus.question: English translations: Abel Boyer (_____); Thomas Brown (1715); R. B. Sheridan and Nathaniel Halhed (1771 and later)
Aristaenetus.fact: English translations: Abel Boyer (1701); Thomas Brown (1715); R. B. Sheridan and Nathaniel Halhed (1771 and later).

Aristagoras.question: The _____ was Greek tyrant of the Ionian city of Miletus (died 497/6 BC).
Aristagoras.fact: Aristagoras of Miletus (Ancient Greek: Ἀρισταγόρας ὁ Μιλήσιος), d.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: 497/496 BC, was the tyrant of the Ionian city of _____ in the late 6th century BC and early 5th century BC
Aristagoras.fact: Aristagoras of Miletus (Ancient Greek: Ἀρισταγόρας ὁ Μιλήσιος), d. 497/496 BC, was the tyrant of the Ionian city of Miletus in the late 6th century BC and early 5th century BC.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: He acted as one of the instigators of the Ionian Revolt against the _____
Aristagoras.fact: He acted as one of the instigators of the Ionian Revolt against the Persian Achaemenid Empire.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: He was the son-in-law of _____ and was granted the tyranny of Miletus from him
Aristagoras.fact: He was the son-in-law of Histiaeus and was granted the tyranny of Miletus from him.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: They shared the coast with the _____ coming in from the Balkans, but neither were prepared for the armed invasion of their lands by the Persians during the late 6th-century BC
Aristagoras.fact: They shared the coast with the Phrygians coming in from the Balkans, but neither were prepared for the armed invasion of their lands by the Persians during the late 6th-century BC.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: The Ionian _____ appealed to the mainland Greeks for assistance and not receiving it were forced to capitulate, becoming subjects of the new Achaemenid Empire
Aristagoras.fact: The Greeks had won the coast of Asia Minor from the preceding Hittite Empire during the Bronze Age, and thanks to their victory at Troy had kept it during the fall of the empire and retirement of the Hittites to Syria. The Ionian Greeks appealed to the mainland Greeks for assistance and not receiving it were forced to capitulate, becoming subjects of the new Achaemenid Empire.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: However, as long as they paid their taxes and were no threat to the rule of the _____, the latter were willing to allow them self-rule under the Greek tyrants
Aristagoras.fact: They shared the coast with the Phrygians coming in from the Balkans, but neither were prepared for the armed invasion of their lands by the Persians during the late 6th-century BC. However, as long as they paid their taxes and were no threat to the rule of the Persians, the latter were willing to allow them self-rule under the Greek tyrants.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: The entire region, however, including those tyrants, held a smoldering resentment against the _____
Aristagoras.fact: The entire region, however, including those tyrants, held a smoldering resentment against the Persian Empire.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: The conspiracy gained the support of many _____ states but failed to win the full support of the mainland Greek states
Aristagoras.fact: The conspiracy gained the support of many Greek Ionian states but failed to win the full support of the mainland Greek states.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: Consequently, the _____ came down upon the Ionian Greeks in overwhelming numbers, sacking the rebel cities, including Miletus
Aristagoras.fact: Consequently, the Persians came down upon the Ionian Greeks in overwhelming numbers, sacking the rebel cities, including Miletus. At Miletus, the Persians killed all the warriors, castrated the young men, and sold the women and children into slavery.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: At Miletus, the _____ killed all the warriors, castrated the young men, and sold the women and children into slavery
Aristagoras.fact: Consequently, the Persians came down upon the Ionian Greeks in overwhelming numbers, sacking the rebel cities, including Miletus. At Miletus, the Persians killed all the warriors, castrated the young men, and sold the women and children into slavery.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: It was their intent that _____ would never again be repopulated, and for some decades it was not
Aristagoras.fact: Consequently, the Persians came down upon the Ionian Greeks in overwhelming numbers, sacking the rebel cities, including Miletus. At Miletus, the Persians killed all the warriors, castrated the young men, and sold the women and children into slavery.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: He would then lay siege to another _____ city, where he and all his men would be killed in combat
Aristagoras.fact: He would then lay siege to another Thracian city, where he and all his men would be killed in combat.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: The first _____ invasion of mainland Greece would occur two years after the defeat of the Ionians
Aristagoras.fact: The first Persian invasion of mainland Greece would occur two years after the defeat of the Ionians. In 492 BC the Persian king Darius would order a naval attack in retaliation against Athens and Eretria for supporting the Greeks in the Ionian Revolt.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: In 492 BC the _____ king Darius would order a naval attack in retaliation against Athens and Eretria for supporting the Greeks in the Ionian Revolt
Aristagoras.fact: The first Persian invasion of mainland Greece would occur two years after the defeat of the Ionians. In 492 BC the Persian king Darius would order a naval attack in retaliation against Athens and Eretria for supporting the Greeks in the Ionian Revolt.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: He was also the son-in-law of _____, whom the Persians had set up as tyrant but did not trust
Aristagoras.fact: He was also the son-in-law of Histiaeus, whom the Persians had set up as tyrant but did not trust. After general Megabazus presented his complaints about Histiaeus to Darius I of Persia, the latter summoned Histiaeus to his court and detained him at Susa, the reason given was that he wanted a trustworthy advisor.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: So he agreed to assist the _____
Aristagoras.fact: Aristagoras considered that if he was able to supply troops to the Naxians, then he could become ruler of Naxos. So he agreed to assist the Naxians.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: He also tempted _____ by adding that capturing the island would place other poleis of the Cyclades under his control
Aristagoras.fact: He explained to Artaphernes that Naxos “was a fine and fertile island, close to the Ionian coast, and rich both in treasures and slaves.” It was also the gateway to the Cyclades, which the Persians did not yet rule. Aristagoras promised that he would both fund the expedition and give Artaphernes a bonus sum.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: They would serve as bases for an invasion of _____
Aristagoras.fact: They would serve as bases for an invasion of Euboea.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: After securing the permission of Susa, _____ agreed and promised 200 ships
Aristagoras.fact: Aristagoras promised that he would both fund the expedition and give Artaphernes a bonus sum. He also tempted Artaphernes by adding that capturing the island would place other poleis of the Cyclades under his control.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: He interfered in _____' role in disciplining the ship captains to save a friend from harsh punishment for an infraction (failure to set a watch on his ship)
Aristagoras.fact: He interfered in Magabates' role in disciplining the ship captains to save a friend from harsh punishment for an infraction (failure to set a watch on his ship).

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: The schism was irreparable with _____ deciding to sabotage the entire operation by secretly informing the Naxians that they were about to be attacked, taking away the element of surprise
Aristagoras.fact: Unfortunately for the success of the invasion, Aristagoras quarreled with the Persian admiral Megabates. The schism was irreparable with Megabates deciding to sabotage the entire operation by secretly informing the Naxians that they were about to be attacked, taking away the element of surprise.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: Four months later, the siege still held, the _____ were out of supplies and had only limited funds remaining
Aristagoras.fact: Four months later, the siege still held, the Persians were out of supplies and had only limited funds remaining. The expedition was then considered a failure and the Persians sailed home.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: The expedition was then considered a failure and the _____ sailed home
Aristagoras.fact: Four months later, the siege still held, the Persians were out of supplies and had only limited funds remaining. The expedition was then considered a failure and the Persians sailed home.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: He began to plan a revolt with the _____ and the other Ionians
Aristagoras.fact: He began to plan a revolt with the Milesians and the other Ionians.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: Meanwhile, _____, still detained at Susa, had tattooed a message upon the shaved head of a slave
Aristagoras.fact: Meanwhile, Histiaeus, still detained at Susa, had tattooed a message upon the shaved head of a slave. Histiaeus, desperate to resume his authority at Miletus, hoped Darius would send him to deal with a Milesian revolt.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: Histiaeus, desperate to resume his authority at _____, hoped Darius would send him to deal with a Milesian revolt
Aristagoras.fact: Histiaeus, desperate to resume his authority at Miletus, hoped Darius would send him to deal with a Milesian revolt. Both leaders being of the same mind, Aristagoras conferred with a council of his supporters, who agreed to a rebellion in Miletus in 499 BC.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: Hecataeus voted against the revolt because he believed that the _____ would be out-matched with defeat being inevitable
Aristagoras.fact: Hecataeus voted against the revolt because he believed that the Ionians would be out-matched with defeat being inevitable. Once the war began, the Ionians expected all to participate, although they could not stop the larger allies from withdrawing.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: Once the war began, the _____ expected all to participate, although they could not stop the larger allies from withdrawing
Aristagoras.fact: Hecataeus voted against the revolt because he believed that the Ionians would be out-matched with defeat being inevitable. Once the war began, the Ionians expected all to participate, although they could not stop the larger allies from withdrawing.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: The Naxos fleet was recovering from its ordeal at _____
Aristagoras.fact: The Naxos fleet was recovering from its ordeal at Myus.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: Ironically, these were mainly _____
Aristagoras.fact: Ironically, these were mainly Greek.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: The scope of the revolt spread rapidly to all _____
Aristagoras.fact: The scope of the revolt spread rapidly to all Ionia. He therefore set about creating an alliance of all the Ionian cities, but the members also came from regions beyond Ionia.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: He therefore set about creating an alliance of all the _____ cities, but the members also came from regions beyond Ionia
Aristagoras.fact: He therefore set about creating an alliance of all the Ionian cities, but the members also came from regions beyond Ionia.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: When his government was in place he sailed to _____ and other states of Greece in search of allies
Aristagoras.fact: When his government was in place he sailed to Lacedaemon and other states of Greece in search of allies.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: There has been some question as to the exact meaning of _____' governmental terms, and as to the form of government of the Ionian alliance
Aristagoras.fact: There has been some question as to the exact meaning of Herodotus' governmental terms, and as to the form of government of the Ionian alliance.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: They were all under the satrapy of Lydia, not under _____
Aristagoras.fact: They were all under the satrapy of Lydia, not under Miletus. The tyrant of Miletus was appointed by the satrap, but he also appointed all the other tyrants.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: The tyrant of _____ was appointed by the satrap, but he also appointed all the other tyrants
Aristagoras.fact: They were all under the satrapy of Lydia, not under Miletus. The tyrant of Miletus was appointed by the satrap, but he also appointed all the other tyrants.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: For reasons not specified in _____, Miletus took the lead
Aristagoras.fact: For reasons not specified in Herodotus, Miletus took the lead.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: The newly sovereign Ionia issued its own coinage between 499 and its destruction by the _____ in 494
Aristagoras.fact: The newly sovereign Ionia issued its own coinage between 499 and its destruction by the Persians in 494.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: He praised the quality of the _____ warriors and argued that a pre-emptive invasion of Persia would be easy
Aristagoras.fact: Aristagoras appealed to the Spartan king, Cleomenes I, for military aid in his revolt. He praised the quality of the Spartan warriors and argued that a pre-emptive invasion of Persia would be easy.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: He also tempted the _____ king with Persian riches
Aristagoras.fact: He praised the quality of the Spartan warriors and argued that a pre-emptive invasion of Persia would be easy. He also tempted the Spartan king with Persian riches.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: At the time, _____ was concerned over possible attacks from the Argives
Aristagoras.fact: He also tempted the Spartan king with Persian riches. When they next met, Cleomenes asked how long it would take to reach Susa, and upon learning that it was a three months’ journey, he firmly refused Spartan assistance as his troops would be gone for too long.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: The Athenians subsequently arrived in _____ with twenty triremes and five others belonging to the Eretrians
Aristagoras.fact: The Athenians subsequently arrived in Miletus with twenty triremes and five others belonging to the Eretrians. Once all his allies had arrived, Aristagoras put his brother Charopinus and another Milesian, Hermophantus, in charge of the expedition, and the whole contingent set out for the provincial capital, Sardis, while Aristagoras remained to govern from Miletus.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: Herodotus described the arrival of these ships as the beginning of troubles between the _____ and the barbarians
Aristagoras.fact: Herodotus described the arrival of these ships as the beginning of troubles between the Greeks and the barbarians.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: The first leg of the journey was to proceed along the coast to _____
Aristagoras.fact: The first leg of the journey was to proceed along the coast to Ephesus.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: Using it as base, they went overland to _____, on which they descended on the city taking its defenders by surprise
Aristagoras.fact: Once all his allies had arrived, Aristagoras put his brother Charopinus and another Milesian, Hermophantus, in charge of the expedition, and the whole contingent set out for the provincial capital, Sardis, while Aristagoras remained to govern from Miletus. Using it as base, they went overland to Sardis, on which they descended on the city taking its defenders by surprise.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: The satrap _____ and his forces retreated to the acropolis immediately
Aristagoras.fact: The satrap Artaphernes and his forces retreated to the acropolis immediately.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: A fire, started allegedly by accident in the town, burned down the temple of the _____ goddess Cybebe (Cybele)
Aristagoras.fact: A fire, started allegedly by accident in the town, burned down the temple of the Lydian goddess Cybebe (Cybele).

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: Attributing the fire to _____ maliciousness, the Persians later used it as an excuse for burning Greek temples
Aristagoras.fact: Attributing the fire to Ionian maliciousness, the Persians later used it as an excuse for burning Greek temples. Interpreting the tumult as a counter-attack, the Ionians retreated to Tmolus, a nearby hill, from which they escaped by night.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: Its defense coincided fortuitously with the arrival of _____ reinforcements
Aristagoras.fact: Attributing the fire to Ionian maliciousness, the Persians later used it as an excuse for burning Greek temples. Its defense coincided fortuitously with the arrival of Persian reinforcements.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: Interpreting the tumult as a counter-attack, the _____ retreated to Tmolus, a nearby hill, from which they escaped by night
Aristagoras.fact: Interpreting the tumult as a counter-attack, the Ionians retreated to Tmolus, a nearby hill, from which they escaped by night. The reinforcements followed the Ionians, caught up with them near Ephesus and soundly defeated them.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: The reinforcements followed the _____, caught up with them near Ephesus and soundly defeated them
Aristagoras.fact: Interpreting the tumult as a counter-attack, the Ionians retreated to Tmolus, a nearby hill, from which they escaped by night. The reinforcements followed the Ionians, caught up with them near Ephesus and soundly defeated them.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: The Persians had conquered _____, including all the Greek cities located in that state
Aristagoras.fact: The Persians had conquered Lydia, including all the Greek cities in that state.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: They made such a show of mercy as to win the hearts and minds of the _____, as well as of some of the Greeks
Aristagoras.fact: They made such a show of mercy as to win the hearts and minds of the Anatolians, as well as of some of the Greeks.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: They arrived with such short notice and major fanfare as to frighten away the Ionian-_____ forces
Aristagoras.fact: They arrived with such short notice and major fanfare as to frighten away the Ionian-Athenian forces.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: The Cambridge Ancient History article attributes this swift arrival to the _____ cavalry, which also had no trouble tracking and catching the Ionians before the gates of Ephesus
Aristagoras.fact: Joint Persian-Anatolian forces hastened overnight to the assistance of the satrap. The Cambridge Ancient History article attributes this swift arrival to the Persian cavalry, which also had no trouble tracking and catching the Ionians before the gates of Ephesus.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: An air of doom pervaded the revolt, but they fought with such spirit that the rebellion spilled over into the nearby _____ islands
Aristagoras.fact: The losses of the mainland Greeks were so great that they sought to return home, leaving Aristagoras and the rebels to fend for themselves. An air of doom pervaded the revolt, but they fought with such spirit that the rebellion spilled over into the nearby Greek islands.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: After this battle, the _____ refused to continue to fight in the Ionian Revolt and returned to Athens
Aristagoras.fact: After this battle, the Athenians refused to continue to fight in the Ionian Revolt and returned to Athens. However, because of Athenians' participation in the revolt, the Persian king, Darius, swore vengeance on Athens and commanded a servant to repeat to him three times every day at dinner, “Master, remember the Athenians”.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: This may only be a story (but not necessarily on that account false), as the _____ intended expansion into the Balkans all along
Aristagoras.fact: This may only be a story (but not necessarily on that account false), as the Persians intended expansion into the Balkans all along. In this last phase of the conflict, almost all of Cyprus also rebelled against the Persians.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: In this last phase of the conflict, almost all of Cyprus also rebelled against the _____
Aristagoras.fact: This may only be a story (but not necessarily on that account false), as the Persians intended expansion into the Balkans all along. In this last phase of the conflict, almost all of Cyprus also rebelled against the Persians.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: The Ionians fought on, gaining control of _____ and the surrounding towns as well as the greater part of Caria
Aristagoras.fact: The Ionians fought on, gaining control of Byzantium and the surrounding towns as well as the greater part of Caria.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: Onesilus, the younger brother of Gorgus, the ruler of _____, tried to convince his brother to rebel against Persia and join in the Ionian Revolt
Aristagoras.fact: Onesilus, the younger brother of Gorgus, the ruler of Salamis, tried to convince his brother to rebel against Persia and join in the Ionian Revolt. When his brother refused to support the revolt, Onesilus waited until he left Salamis and then shut the city gates on him.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: When his brother refused to support the revolt, _____ waited until he left Salamis and then shut the city gates on him
Aristagoras.fact: Onesilus, the younger brother of Gorgus, the ruler of Salamis, tried to convince his brother to rebel against Persia and join in the Ionian Revolt. When his brother refused to support the revolt, Onesilus waited until he left Salamis and then shut the city gates on him.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: Gorgus fled to the _____ while Onesilus took over and convinced the Cyprians to revolt
Aristagoras.fact: In this last phase of the conflict, almost all of Cyprus also rebelled against the Persians. Gorgus fled to the Persians while Onesilus took over and convinced the Cyprians to revolt.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: They then proceeded to lay siege to the city of _____
Aristagoras.fact: They then proceeded to lay siege to the city of Amathus.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: He and his men resolved on _____ in Thrace, which had been an Ionian stronghold in the abortive Persian invasion of Scythia
Aristagoras.fact: He and his men resolved on Myrcinus in Thrace, which had been an Ionian stronghold in the abortive Persian invasion of Scythia.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: The Thracians, not now disposed to tolerate any further presence of _____ in their country, opposed this incursion
Aristagoras.fact: The Thracians, not now disposed to tolerate any further presence of Greeks in their country, opposed this incursion.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: By an accidental sequence of historical events his reputation drew the ire of his main historian, _____ of Halicarnassus, an Ionian partisan, to such a degree that it suffers yet
Aristagoras.fact: By an accidental sequence of historical events his reputation drew the ire of his main historian, Herodotus of Halicarnassus, an Ionian partisan, to such a degree that it suffers yet.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: In the last months of the failing revolt, the _____ were reconquering the rebel Ionians city by city
Aristagoras.fact: In the last months of the failing revolt, the Persians were reconquering the rebel Ionians city by city.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: When all was nearly lost, the _____ king Darius was convinced by Histiaeus that he could settle the conflict and now should be sent back to Miletus
Aristagoras.fact: Expecting a swift Persian victory, Aristagoras had hoped to establish a redoubt of Ionians, who would come to the assistance of Miletus at a later time. In the last months of the failing revolt, the Persians were reconquering the rebel Ionians city by city.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: Histiaeus never succeeded in reaching _____
Aristagoras.fact: When all was nearly lost, the Persian king Darius was convinced by Histiaeus that he could settle the conflict and now should be sent back to Miletus. Histiaeus never succeeded in reaching Miletus.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: Reporting first to _____, whether with or without the Great King's complicity (Herodotus does not say), he was interrogated concerning his true loyalties
Aristagoras.fact: Reporting first to Sardis, whether with or without the Great King's complicity (Herodotus does not say), he was interrogated concerning his true loyalties.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: Histiaeus swore complete ignorance of the events of the revolt and unquestionable loyalty to the _____
Aristagoras.fact: Histiaeus swore complete ignorance of the events of the revolt and unquestionable loyalty to the Persians.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: He admitted nothing, but the satrap, _____, was not in the least deceived
Aristagoras.fact: He admitted nothing, but the satrap, Artaphernes, was not in the least deceived. He said, "I will tell thee how the case stands, Histaeus: this shoe is of thy stitching; Aristagoras has but put it on." Recognizing that he risked arrest or worse at the hands of Artaphernes, Histiaeus escaped that night and took ship at the coast, probably at Ephesus.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: He had no trouble raising troops and finding ships, but he found that he was not trusted by the _____
Aristagoras.fact: He had no trouble raising troops and finding ships, but he found that he was not trusted by the Ionians.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: He became a mercenary in the _____ until he was hunted down and executed by Artaphernes
Aristagoras.fact: He became a mercenary in the Aegean until he was hunted down and executed by Artaphernes.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: The Persians went on to prepare for the conquest of _____ under the pretext of a punitive campaign against Athens
Aristagoras.fact: The Persians went on to prepare for the conquest of Greece under the pretext of a punitive campaign against Athens.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: Due to the disparity in resources and the reluctance of the mainland Greek states to involve themselves, the _____ failed and Persia regained control over the Ionian Greeks
Aristagoras.fact: The Ionian Revolt finally ended in 494/493 BC. Due to the disparity in resources and the reluctance of the mainland Greek states to involve themselves, the Ionian Revolt failed and Persia regained control over the Ionian Greeks.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: After only one year, the _____ were once again forced into submission by Persia
Aristagoras.fact: After only one year, the Cyprians were once again forced into submission by Persia.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: The cities around the _____ fell one after another to Daurises, the son-in-law of king Darius
Aristagoras.fact: The cities around the Hellespont fell one after another to Daurises, the son-in-law of king Darius.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: The Carians fought the _____ at the Meander River and were defeated with severe casualties
Aristagoras.fact: The Carians fought the Persians at the Meander River and were defeated with severe casualties. Aiming directly for Miletus in 494 BC, the Persians defeated the Ionians in the naval Battle of Lade, an island off Miletus.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT
Aristagoras.question: Cyprus was recaptured by _____ and Phoenician forces
Aristagoras.fact: The Carians fought the Persians at the Meander River and were defeated with severe casualties. Cyprus was recaptured by Persian and Phoenician forces.

Aristagoras.subject: Computer & IT

ASCII.subject: Computer & IT
ASCII.question: What is ASCII? Character encoding standard.
ASCII.fact: ASCII ( ASS-kee), an acronym for American Standard Code for Information Interchange, is a character encoding standard for representing a particular set of 95 (English-language–focused) printable and 33 control characters – a total of 128 code points.   ASCII hugely influenced the design of character sets used by modern computers; for example, the first 128 code points of Unicode are the same as ASCII.

ASCII art.subject: Computer & IT
ASCII art.question: The _____ was Computer art form using text characters.
ASCII art.fact: ASCII art is a graphic design technique that uses computers for presentation and consists of pictures pieced together from the 95 printable (from a total of 128) characters defined by the ASCII Standard from 1963 and ASCII compliant character sets with proprietary extended characters (beyond the 128 characters of standard 7-bit ASCII). ASCII art can be created with any text editor, and is often used with free-form languages.
